fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for an Affiliate Program
fields.features_subheading: Each program runs as one app with its own sign-up form and records, and every balance traces back to its orders.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the program, get the app

Emergent builds the sign-up form and the commission rules, with the affiliate database behind them, from a plain-English prompt. When a rate changes, ask for it in a new prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Orders from Stripe, affiliates in HubSpot

The app connects to any tool with an API. It reads each Stripe order with its referral code, and syncs approved affiliates to HubSpot so your partner team works from one list.
fields.feature_3:
A nudge when a person has to decide

The app sends a Slack message when an application falls under your traffic minimum, and an email reminder if the payout run still waits for approval two days after the 1st.
fields.feature_4:
W-9s on file before the first payout

The app asks each US affiliate for a W-9 and keeps payment records ready for 1099 reporting. It organizes the data for your accountant; it does not file taxes for you.
fields.feature_5:
Every commission in a database you own

Each referred order and the commission it earned is a row in a database you own. There is no task cap, and a launch week with 3,000 referred orders runs like any other week.
fields.feature_6:
The code goes to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code of your affiliate app to your GitHub repository. A developer can add a custom credit rule or move hosting without rebuilding the program.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Affiliate Programs Run Their Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
Bracklin Kitchen gets its code after clearing 10,000 visitors

An application from the Bracklin Kitchen blog reaches Corvelle Tea Company with 42,000 monthly visitors, clearing the 10,000-visitor minimum. The app approves the blog and sends a welcome email with its referral link and the code BRACKLINTEA. Sites under 10,000 wait for the affiliate manager, Kerensa Pembridge.
fields.tab_content_2:
Theo's $36 commission is reversed after the day 12 return

Order #8817 for $240 comes in to Moorcastle Leather through Theo Grainger's referral link. The app credits Theo a $36 commission and holds it for the 30-day refund window. On day 12 the customer returns the bag and Stripe records the refund. The app reverses the $36 and emails Theo the order number.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two payouts for $598.50 wait for Adaeze to approve

On the 1st, Maravel Cycling's app totals each affiliate's approved commissions. Lowgear Commutes is owed $412.50 and Cadence Club $186.00, a $598.50 run that waits for the finance lead, Adaeze Okafor-Vane, to approve. Fernhill Rides has $38.00, under the $50 minimum, and that balance rolls into next month.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 214 links checked, 3 go to Wes

Every Monday morning the app checks the 214 affiliate links in Trailcairn Reviews' gear posts. Three return an error this week, including a 404 on the two-person tent review. The editor, Wes Quiller, gets a Slack message listing every broken link with its post.

fields.howto_title: How to Automate an Affiliate Program
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to put your commission rules in writing and build affiliate automation that credits each sale and pays it out.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set the floor for automatic approval
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Choose how a sale gets credited
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the program in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put every rule on one page before you build: the commission rate for each product line, how long a commission is held, the payout minimum, and the day payouts run. A rule nobody wrote down turns into an argument with an affiliate later.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick one number that approves an affiliate on its own, such as monthly visitors or newsletter subscribers, and set the floor. Every application under it goes to a named person. Start with a low floor and raise it once you see which affiliates sell.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what happens when a buyer clicks one affiliate's link and then types another affiliate's discount code. Write down which one wins, and whether the first click or the last click counts. The app follows exactly the rule you write.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write the prompt the way you would brief a new partnerships hire: the sign-up questions, the rules from step one, and who gets each alert. Emergent builds the form, the records, and the commission logic from that description.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Connect your store and your CRM
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect the tools that hold your orders and your affiliate contacts, such as Stripe for payments and HubSpot for partner records. Each commission the app calculates is written back to your database next to the order that earned it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before any affiliate sees a number, run last month's orders through the app and compare its commissions with what you paid by hand. Any order where the two disagree points to a rule that needs rewording in the prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Approve the first payout runs yourself
fields.howto_step_7_des: Keep a person on the first few payout runs. Read the list on the 1st, check the balances that rolled over, and approve the run in the app. Once three runs match your own math, hand approval to your finance lead.

faq_plan.a: Affiliate automation is software that runs the repeatable parts of an affiliate program: approving applicants, crediting each sale to the affiliate who referred it, holding and reversing commissions, and totaling payouts. People keep the judgment calls, such as which partners to recruit and what to do about a suspicious order.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up affiliate automation?
faq_plan.a: Write your commission rules down first, then describe the program to Emergent's AI automation builder in plain English: the sign-up questions, the commission rate, the hold period, and the payout minimum. Emergent builds the app from that prompt. When a rule changes later, such as a new rate for one product line, a new prompt changes it.

faq_plan.q: Which affiliate tasks can automation handle?
faq_plan.a: The ones that follow a rule: crediting sales, holding commissions through refunds, totaling payouts, and checking links. Recruiting partners and writing honest reviews stay with people.

faq_plan.q: How long should affiliate automation hold a commission before payout?
faq_plan.a: Hold each commission at least as long as your refund window. If customers can return an order within 30 days, a 30-day hold means a returned order's commission is reversed before it is ever paid out. Emergent changes the hold with a new prompt when your return policy changes.

faq_plan.q: Who gets credit in affiliate automation when a link and a coupon code conflict?
faq_plan.a: Whichever one your rule names. Pick one before launch: the coupon code wins because the buyer typed it on purpose, or the link wins because it brought the buyer to the site. Tell affiliates which rule you chose in the welcome email.

faq_plan.q: What application details should affiliate automation approve on?
faq_plan.a: Approve on the details that decide fit: the site or channel, the audience number you set a floor on, the niche, and how the applicant plans to promote you. Send anything that needs judgment to a person. Collect the payout details and the W-9 after approval, on a second form.

Yes. Have the app compare each referred order with the affiliate's own account: the same email, the same shipping address, or the same card's last four digits. Then have it hold a matching order's commission and send it to a person to decide, instead of reversing it on its own.

faq_plan.q: Can affiliate automation find broken affiliate links?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app requests every affiliate link on a schedule and records the status code and the page it finally lands on. A 404 is plainly broken. A redirect to the store's home page can mean the product was taken down. Flag those for a person to check as well.

faq_plan.q: Where does affiliate automation store commission data?
faq_plan.a: In the app's own database, which is the record you settle any dispute from. With Emergent, each commission and the order behind it sit in a database you own, and paid plans can export the full code to your GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: How does affiliate automation tell affiliates a commission was reversed?
faq_plan.a: It sends a message at each status change with the order number and the reason, which answers the question before the affiliate writes in. The app Emergent builds can send each notice by email or as an in-app alert on the affiliate's dashboard.
